text:
Anthropic released the Claude 4 family, consisting of two models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. This dual-model strategy positioned Opus 4 as the flagship model with pricing at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens, while positioning Sonnet 4 as a faster "workhorse" developer-default coding model priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled that agentic coding was becoming the defining product category for AI in 2025, specifically timed to coincide with the rise of Claude Code [Source: ev-1]. By introducing these models, Anthropic aimed to lead an enterprise "agentic-coding gold rush," competing directly against OpenAI’s o-series by positioning its offerings as the safest and most reliable coding agents [Source: ev-1]. The release highlighted significant improvements in reliability, noting that the new "computer use 2.0" capability was roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation's features [Source: ev-1]. This strategic move successfully cemented Anthropic's position as a leader in the market, contributing to record API usage and supporting a large funding round in late September 2025 at a reported valuation of approximately $183 billion [Source: ev-1].
